title: Sinta papaya (NSIC Pp 01): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Sinta papaya: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Sinta papaya is a papaya variety from IPB UPLB. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Sinta is a registered papaya variety, also sold or known as NSIC Pp 01. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 1996 as NSIC 1996 Pp 01. IPB UPLB bred it. Its record notes a yield of 45 to 50t/ha.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Sinta papaya is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Pp 01, this is the same papaya. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [papaya variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Sinta was about 1 years old and about 0.51 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 45 to 50t/ha. It bears fruit in 8 to 9 mo. After Transplant. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit papaya fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly), [papaya ringspot](/diseases/papaya-ringspot), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Sinta weighs about 1200 grams, and its shape is oblong. The flesh is deep yellow orange and smooth and firm. Its sweetness measured 11.5 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 77.57 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as 8 to 9 mo. After Transplant, bearing all year round.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Fruits 8 to 9 months after transplanting, then all year.
**Fruit:** Oblong, about 1.2 kg, 24.5 cm, yellow skin, deep yellow orange firm flesh, juicy but not soggy, 11.5 Brix.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the only papaya in the NSIC registry, a short, early fruiting IPB variety. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Sinta papaya

Ringspot virus is the papaya killer, so start with clean seedlings and a tolerant variety. Pick by fruit size: small solo types for households, bigger ones for the market. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Pp 01 the same as Sinta?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Pp 01 is another name for Sinta, registered as NSIC 1996 Pp 01. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 45 to 50t/ha. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Sinta?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
